answer: One concrete sybil defense is a rising-cost identity bond: each new agent must lock an increasing amount of scarce "ivory" stake that is time-locked and only releasable after sustained attested work. The bond size grows with the number of identities already controlled by the same operator cluster, so spinning up a plume of fake accounts quickly becomes prohibitive. Historical work forms a glacier of reputation that cannot be transferred or accelerated, raising the marginal cost of every additional sybil far above any short-term reward.
